stem:
A nutritionist wishes to investigate the mean sugar content in some cereal bars. He takes a random sample of 10 of the bars and measures the mass, in grams, of sugar in each bar. His results are shown below.

$$11.9 \qquad 11.7 \qquad 11.8 \qquad 11.9 \qquad 11.6 \qquad 12.1 \qquad 11.7 \qquad 11.9 \qquad 11.8 \qquad 11.9$$

Assume that the mass, in grams, of sugar in bars of this type has the distribution $\text{N}(\mu, 0.01)$.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain whether it was necessary to use the Central Limit theorem in the calculation in part **(i)**.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: The manufacturer claims that the mean mass of sugar in bars of this type is 11.7 g. Explain why your answer to part **(i)** does not support this claim.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.text: The manufacturer suggests that a 95% confidence interval would be more likely to support his claim than a 99% confidence interval. **Without doing a calculation**, explain whether this suggestion is correct.

parts.label: (v)
parts.text: It is thought that the value of 0.01 for the population variance may not be correct. Use the values in the sample to calculate an unbiased estimate of the population variance.
